## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing the scatter-render into the per-particle step eliminates intermediates and can approach the streaming ceiling despite byte-granular framebuffer writes.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p FALLS from 11.898 at N=4000 (above the L1d spill at N≈963, within L2) to 7.676 at N=65000 (at the L2 spill point N≈61680), reflecting fixed prologue/epilogue overhead being amortized as per-particle work dominates. From N=65000 through N=4000000 the cost stays FLAT at ~7.66 ns/p — no knee appears at the L2→DRAM transition (working set 4.4 MB → 272 MB), indicating the algo is not streaming-bandwidth-limited. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.05 holds ~8.1–8.2 ns/p and q=0.25 holds ~10.3 ns/p across the same N range, confirming the scatter/respawn cost is per-particle overhead, not cache-pressure-driven.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 8.93 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 35.4% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.25 it falls to 6.61 GB/s (26%). The algo is overhead/scatter-bound, not bandwidth-bound: the flat ns/p from N=65000 to N=4000000 (7.676→7.659) shows no DRAM-bandwidth knee, and achieved BW never exceeds 36% of ceiling at any N or death rate. The transition is by death rate, not by N — rising q monotonically depresses BW from 8.93 to 6.58 GB/s as the branchy respawn path executes more frequently.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of a single particle, not across particles: `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` update four packed floats of one particle's position/velocity, with `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` rearranging lanes within that particle. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads a single scalar element into a vector lane from a particle field. The render scatter is entirely scalar byte-granular: 19 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` instructions perform framebuffer writes/reads, each followed by `cmp #0xff` / `csel` saturation clamps (18 csel total). This byte-granular scatter — not the vectorized particle update — caps bandwidth at 35% of ceiling: the `strb` stores cannot coalesce into cache-line streaming traffic, and the per-pixel clamp chain serializes the render loop.

## Verdict
Refuted — the fused scatter-render never exceeds 8.93 GB/s (35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate, and the flat ns/p from N=65000 to N=4000000 (7.676→7.659) confirms the bottleneck is the byte-granular `strb` scatter and saturation clamps, not streaming bandwidth. Death rate raises the floor from 7.66 to 10.33 ns/p (q=0.01→0.25) via the branchy `bl spawn` respawn path but never changes the N-shape, so the hypothesis fails across all regimes.
